[0] everyday_reading (E): In the everyday sense, a 'program' includes its data, so changing the results means editing the code. In data-driven code the data live in files read from standard input, so they change while the program stays the same.

[0] names_the_element (N): Data-driven code is a design style: data are kept in files and the program reads them from standard input, so the data can change without changing the program.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Keep the data in files and write programs that read from standard input. Then change the data, not the program.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): The program is launched with `< file`. It reads values in file order and interprets them by a format convention (e.g. a header first, then records) until isEmpty().
[1] output_prediction (OP): The same program with different files gives different outputs. `java PlayThatTune < elise.txt` plays Für Elise, and another file plays another tune.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Each read takes the next value from the data file, where a literal written in the code would otherwise be.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Redirecting a different data file to standard input changes what the unchanged program processes.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Data-driven code lets one program serve many data sets (experiments, transactions, web models). It is the norm in data processing.

[0] predict_a_change (C): Changing the data file keeps the program and its correctness. Changing the file's format (field order, header) breaks the program's reads.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use data-driven code when the same computation must run on many or changing data sets. Values that are intrinsic to the algorithm belong in the code, and a few launch parameters go on the command line.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The data file must follow the program's input format. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: A file with a non-numeric token, or fields in the wrong order: NumberFormatException at the read.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The data file must contain all the values the program reads. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: A truncated file (fewer values than a header promises): the read after the end fails.
Redirecting a file to standard input lets the same program process different data files without being changed.
